title: Machine-learning immune phenotypes link STK11/KEAP1 co-mutations to prognosis in NSCLC
summary: A machine-learning model classified resected stage I-IIIA NSCLC tumors as inflamed, altered or desert from the spatial distribution of CD8+ T cells in 934 patients (453 prospective, 481 retrospective): 24.4%, 51.3% and 24.3% respectively. KEAP1 (OR 0.27) and STK11 (OR 0.39) were co-mutated in non-inflamed lung adenocarcinoma, and in the retrospective cohort the inflamed phenotype predicted longer disease-specific survival (HR 0.61, P = 0.01). These are associations, not causal evidence.
ai_technology: Machine-learning classifier of CD8+ T-cell spatial distribution into immune phenotypes
organization: Brigham and Women's Hospital; University Hospital of North Norway; Harvard University

evidence.tested: Immune phenotypes were related to NanoString gene expression, panel sequencing and survival in two surgical cohorts.
evidence.unknown: Causality and model development details are not given in the abstract. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: ML assigned each tumor to an immune phenotype from CD8+ T-cell spatial distribution, enabling the genomic and survival associations.
